### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hypomaturation-hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta with taurodontism  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.741)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2916)

**Proposed mechanism:** DLX3 (HGNC:2916) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of odontoblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production (GO:0042571); Regulation of odontoblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production (GO:0042571) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal tooth enamel morphology (HP:0000923); Regulation of odontoblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production (GO:0042571) —LEADS_TO→ Hair abnormalities (HP:0001077); Regulation of odontoblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production (GO:0042571) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal bone morphology (HP:0000924). Loss-of-function mutations in DLX3 disrupt the normal regulation of odontoblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production, leading to abnormal tooth enamel morphology (hypomaturation-hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta with taurodontism). These disruptions also affect hair and bone development, manifesting as tricho-dento-osseous syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in DLX3 with a consistent loss-of-function effect in patients with hypomaturation-hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta with taurodontism, but not in those with tricho-dento-osseous syndrome, or vice versa, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in DLX3 are absent or extremely rare in the general population (gnomAD).)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of DLX3 in these distinct but related craniofacial and ectodermal phenotypes could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies for improving dental and skeletal outcomes in both conditions.
